Writing in Puck , Matthew Belloni suggests that the favourable contract terms he says have been offered to Pattinson suggest that the actor, currently in cinemas with reality-crime thriller Primetime , is studio Amazon MGM’s preferred choice for the role. articles.title: Heartland review – Jessica Chastain’s Netflix country music thriller is more miss than hit
articles.summary: The Oscar winner plays a singer turned detective searching for her niece in an overly generic Nashville-based mystery that fails to find its footing Given the popularity of its music and the streaming services’ interest in faith-based programming, I’m always a little surprised that there aren’t more movies and TV shows about Nashville. Well, at least the idea of Nashville, the country music mecca that is perpetually struggling to define itself within and against the country at large, a place that has always been more diverse than its reputation yet still stands for a certain image of white, Christian Americana. articles.title: The Body review – this sexy retro high school drama is like Cruel Intentions … with added Satanic rituals
articles.summary: This coming-of-age tale of Catholic school girls is gleefully camp from the off – and full of fun references to its 2004 setting. And then a Halloween party goes wrong… What’s more judgmental than a teenage girl? Easy: the Catholic church. Deliciously, Netflix’s new YA drama The Body has both in equal measure. It’s Halloween 2004 at St Mark’s Catholic school and the social hierarchy is exactly as you would expect. Perched at the top is the dance troupe, the Lions, presided over by Anya (Kristina Bogic) and Elise (Sara Boustany), two best friends skirting around their sexual chemistry. The show’s resident outcasts are Lisbeth (Geena Meszaros) and Leo (Jackson Kelly), previously homeschooled siblings who live a limited existence with their unwell mother. articles.title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: acrobatic Lagos producer Azzi on the Beat
articles.summary: An innovator in mara, the fast, sample-heavy dance music of neighbourhood parties, the Nigerian has made a debut album that will be relentlessly energising From Lagos, Nigeria Recommended if you like Rema, Blnde, Zinoleesky Up next Debut album Mara Gram, released 12 November; plays Nyege Nyege festival , Uganda, 19–22 November Azzi on the Beat doesn’t exactly ease listeners into Mara Gram. On its opening track Police Way, sirens blare, drums clatter and another rhythm seems to barge in before the first has finished. This is mara, the fast, sample-heavy dance music that grew out of carnivals and neighbourhood parties in working-class Lagos, with tempos reaching 160 beats per minute. Continue reading...

articles.title: The Areni-1 Cave Shoe in Yerevan, Armenia
articles.summary: This leather shoe was discovered in Areni 1 cave during excavations in 2008. Made from a single piece of cowhide leather, and still with its leather laces it has been measured as corresponding to a modern US size 7 / EU size 37 / UK size 6. It is stuffed with grass to either maintain its shape or keep the foot warm. It is unknown at this stage whether it was a man or woman's shoe. Researchers have managed to date it back to 3600-3500 BC based on the radiocarbon dating. The shoe managed to survive in near-perfect condition because of the cool, dry cave environment which was sealed off by several layers of sheep dung. The shoe was found upside down at the base of a shallow, rounded, and plastered pit, beneath an overturned broken Chalcolithic ceramic bowl.

articles.title: Pensão Amor in Lisbon, Portugal
articles.summary: Walk down Pink Street in Lisbon’s Cais do Sodré and you’ll eventually find a door that looks like it has secrets. Pensão Amor building is a former brothel that has been transformed into a surprising space in Lisbon's port district. Cais do Sodré was once the sailors’ quarter, where seamen fresh off the boats mingled with writers, fado singers, artists, prostitutes and the occasional spy. Pensão Amor takes that cast of characters and gives them a party. The bar is a riot of velvet, red light, and cheerful mischief. On any given night, you might catch burlesque, pole dancing, live music, poetry, or theater, sometimes all in the same week. Nobody here is trying to hide what the building used to be. articles.title: Sue Metal T-Rex Statue in Faith, South Dakota
articles.summary: At the edge of the South Dakota prairie, a scrap-metal Tyrannosaurus rex rises from the small town of Faith. A tribute to one of the most famous dinosaurs ever unearthed. Built from recycled tractors and agricultural materials, this sculpture honors Sue, the largest and most complete T. rex fossil discovered in the United States. The original skeleton now resides in Chicago's Field Museum. Faith proudly calls itself the "T. rex Capital of the World," a title rooted in the fossil-rich lands nearby. Sue was discovered on August 12, 1990, by fossil hunter Sue Hendrickson while working with the Black Hills Institute on the Cheyenne River Reservation. articles.title: Xuan Phong Church in Tuy Phuoc Dong, Vietnam
articles.summary: Rising out of the rural landscapes of Tuy Phuoc, Xuan Phong Church presents an intriguing architectural cross-pollination that defies conventional ecclesiastical design. Originally established as a modest thatched sanctuary in the late nineteenth century, the current structure was erected around 1890 using repurposed ancient Cham bricks salvaged from the nearby Binh Lam area, creating a tangible physical bridge between Catholic history and the region's medieval Champa heritage. Most striking is its facade, dominated by three towering spires whose tapered geometric profiles distinctly mirror the iconic silhouette of traditional Cham towers, while church archives have also drawn structural comparisons to Khmer temple architecture.
